channel.title: Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Radio Free Europe / Radio Liberty (rferl.org)

item.title: Then And Now: Life For Afghan Women Since The 2021 Taliban Takeover
item.description: For many Afghan women, especially those in conservative rural areas of the country, little has changed since the Taliban seized power in the country. For others, life under hard-line Islamist rule today looks vastly different from the two decades the country spent under US and NATO intervention.

item.title: Tehran Skyline Blanketed In Smoke Following Strikes On Oil Facilities
item.description: The Tehran skyline was filled with smoke following Israeli strikes on oil facilities in Iran. The Israeli military claimed responsibility for strikes on a number of fuel storage facilities in Tehran on March 8.

item.title: Israeli Opposition Leader Yair Lapid Tells RFE/RL Iran's Oil ‘Lifeline' Must Be Cut
item.description: Yair Lapid, the leader of the opposition in Israel, says air strikes on Iranian oil fields --which have showered Tehran in black rain -- were needed to cut the “lifeline of the regime” in Iran.

item.title: Trump Says Iran Campaign To End 'Very Soon,' Disappointed In Choice Of Khamenei's Son
item.description: US President Donald Trump said the military operation launched against Iran last month will end "very soon" and vowed to hit the country "much, much harder" if it blocks oil supplies in the Middle East.

item.title: Sleeping In A Tel Aviv Subway Station Takes Its Toll
item.description: Israelis without bomb shelters at home have been sleeping for more than a week now in underground railway stations in Tel Aviv, amid constant alerts of incoming Iranian ballistic missiles. RFE/RL’s Ray Furlong joined them.

item.title: 'Death To Mojtaba' Chants Heard As Iran Picks New Supreme Leader
item.description: Chanting against Iran's newly appointed supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, could be heard in video posted on social media. Voices chanting "Death to Mojtaba" echoed through buildings in a Tehran residential neighborhood on March 8.

item.title: Sleeping On A Subway Platform To Evade Iranian Missiles In Tel Aviv
item.description: For Aviad Apirion, a 40-year-old teacher in a special needs school, the war with Iran has meant sleeping every night at an underground railway station to avoid the danger of incoming Iranian ballistic missiles.

item.title: In Ukraine's Donbas, A Lovers' Kiss Becomes A Symbol Of War's Grim March
item.description: Just months ago, weddings were celebrated around a statue to young lovers in Ukraine’s eastern city of Druzhkivka. Today the monument is surrounded by ever-increasing destruction as Russian forces use long-range first-person-view drones and aerial bombs on the industrial city.

item.title: 'Save Our Girls': Five Iranian Female Soccer Players Reportedly Seek Asylum In Australia
item.description: After the Iranian women's soccer team declined to sing along with their country's anthem at an Asian Cup game, an Iranian state TV presenter denounced them as "wartime traitors." Fearing for their safety, five of the players reportedly left their training camp in Australia on March 9 to seek asylum.

item.title: Trump: If Iran Disrupts Oil, US Will Hit '20 Times Harder'
item.description: As the US-Israeli war with Iran continues to impact and shape the region, journalists from RFE/RL deliver ongoing updates and analysis.
